title: Giwa (Verdun) Review: Pretty Plates, Subtle Korean Twists, and a Waterfront Walk After

blocks.text: Giwa is the kind of place you pick when you want Korean food that feels a little more polished than your usual go-to, but still relaxed. The plates show up looking sharp, the technique is there, and the menu plays with classics in a way that feels modern without getting weird about it.

One honest note: the flavors lean a bit toned down (more refined than loud). If you’re chasing maximum heat, funk, or punch, you might wish it went harder. But if you want a pretty, easy night where the food still feels thoughtful, it’s a really solid date move.
Giwa
**Location:** Montreal
**Price Range:** $$-$$$ (mid-range; “nice night out” without full fine-dining pressure)
**Cuisine:** Korean classics with a modern twist
**Dress Code:** Casual to Smart Casual
**Quick Verdict:**

items: Best For: Low-stress date nights, pretty plates, “let’s try something different” energy
Conversation Friendly: 4/5 (casual, comfortable)
Ambiance: Casual Korean restaurant vibe (terrasse is the move in summer)
Reservation: Recommended (especially for terrasse nights)

blocks.text: The Vibe

Inside, it feels like a classic casual Korean restaurant: welcoming, straightforward, and not pretending to be fine dining. That’s exactly why it works for dates. You can focus on your person, not on “doing the restaurant correctly.”
We didn’t get a full look at the interior because we sat on the **terrasse**, and if the weather’s good, I’d recommend doing the same. It instantly turns dinner into a proper Montréal night.
**Lighting:** Natural / outdoor-friendly (terrasse), otherwise casual
**Noise Level:** Low-to-medium (more “neighborhood dinner” than “party room”)
**Best Seats:** Terrasse for date-night ease; inside if you want the full atmosphere
What to Order (Date-Night Game Plan)
This is a “share a few things” spot. Order in layers so the table keeps changing while you talk.
**Easy order for two:**

items: 2 appetizers (they’re the easiest to share)
1 dish from the main menu
1 dish from the seasonal menu
1 sot bap (even if you’re not usually a sot bap person, it’s their specialty)
Dessert: either 1 dessert + ice cream, or 2 plated desserts if you’re in a sweet mood

blocks.text: I didn’t order the sot bap myself, and in hindsight, I probably should have. Giwa actually won a bibimbap competition in Montreal during the Korean Festival 2026, judged by Edward Lee (yes, that Edward Lee from Culinary Wars). That’s a pretty strong hint that this is the thing to try.
**How to order (so it feels like a date, not a rush):**

items: Start with something light + bright
Follow with one comforting classic
Add one “twist” dish that shows the chef’s point of view

blocks.text: What to order if you like…

items: **Classics (comfort + familiarity):** pick one or two staples you already know, then see how Giwa refines them.
**Twists (chef energy):** choose at least one seasonal/local-leaning dish.
**Pretty plating:** say yes to anything that looks like it’s meant to be photographed.

blocks.text: What I Ordered (and what it’s like)

items: **Gimbap:** seaweed roll with fish of the moment, cucumber, avocado, and a gochujang vinaigrette. **Flavor:** fresh, lightly sweet, gently spicy, and super clean. Great first bite and easy to share.
**Yukhwe:** beef tartare with pear, sesame, soy sauce, egg yolk, and nasturtium. **Flavor:** sweet-salty, silky, and rich, with juicy pear cutting through and sesame/soy giving it that savory depth.

**Haemul Jang:** soy-marinated seafood (crab, shrimp, octopus, salmon) with seaweed and egg yolk. **Flavor:** briny-sweet seafood + soy umami, with the egg yolk making it feel glossy and rich. (One downside: the seaweed crisp element didn’t feel as fresh/crispy as it should have.)

blocks.text: **Would I reorder it?** Probably not. It’s tempting and worth trying once, but for the price (seafood isn’t cheap), the flavor felt a bit uniform and toned down. It leaned heavily soy-forward, and I wanted more contrast and punch.

items: **Baechu (seasonal):** charred napa cabbage glazed with doenjang, served over perilla cream with cucumber and fresh herbs. **Flavor:** smoky-sweet cabbage, savory doenjang funk, and a cooling, herbal finish from the perilla + cucumber.

blocks.text: Dessert

items: **Doenjang crème brûlée:** **Flavor:** sweet + salty, with that fermented doenjang edge that’s a little unfamiliar. Cleanly done, but not my vibe. I wouldn’t reorder this one.
**Basque corn cheesecake** with torched corn + corn ice cream. **Flavor:** creamy, toasty, sweet-corn dessert energy. (Note: the popcorn topping tasted a bit stale.)

**Hodumaru (my pick):** rich gochujang chocolate mousse + chili-spiked chantilly, candied walnuts, and maple ice cream. **Flavor:** chocolate-forward with a warm chili tingle, crunchy-nutty top, and sweet maple creaminess to round it out.
**Makgeolli sorbet:** a clean, lightly boozy, gently tangy palate reset to finish.

blocks.text: Food & Plating
This is where Giwa really shines.

items: **Plating is genuinely pretty**: clean, modern, and photo-friendly.
The menu hits **Korean classics with a twist**, and the technique shows.
The only “but”: the overall flavor intensity can feel **a bit toned down**. It’s polished, not aggressive.
A couple of elements felt **prepped too far ahead**: the seaweed crisp didn’t have that fresh snap, and the popcorn on the dessert tasted a bit stale.

blocks.text: A nice detail I really liked: they lean into a **seasonal menu** and call out **local products**, so it doesn’t feel like the same old greatest hits.
Service
Service is casual and easy: friendly, low-pressure, and aligned with the vibe. It felt like the kind of place where you can take your time without feeling rushed.
Drinks
The drink list has interesting choices, but it didn’t blow me away.
We had:

items: **Somaek:** fresh soju + Origine lager. **Flavor:** crisp, clean, and light.
**Omija:** gin, five-flavor berry syrup, lemon. **Flavor:** bright and fruity-tart, very easy to drink.

blocks.text: If you’re doing date night properly, start with one drink to settle in while you decide what to share.
**Date tip:** One drink each at the start, then switch to water or tea. It keeps the night light and the conversation flowing.
The Real Cost (So You Can Plan)
**Per Person:** ~$90 (CAD, based on our meal)
**Worth it?** Yes if you care about technique and plating, and you want Korean flavors that feel approachable.
**Save money:** Skip the second round of drinks and add one more dish to share instead. More fun, more food memories.
Before/After Dating Spots Nearby (Dating Concept)
Make it a plan with one simple add-on. These are real, easy Verdun moves.
**Before dinner (pick one):**

items: Walk **Promenade Wellington** for 10-15 minutes (window-shop, people-watch, show up hungry)
Golden-hour stroll along the **Verdun waterfront** (Fleuve Saint-Laurent), especially around **Parc Arthur-Therrien**
If you’re coming from downtown, make it a mini “destination” by meeting in Verdun and walking Wellington together

blocks.text: **After dinner (pick one):**

items: A gentle **Promenade Wellington** walk (best “keep talking” move)
Walk down to the **Verdun waterfront** again and sit for a few minutes (quiet, romantic, no pressure)
If you want a “second location” that still feels easy: grab a nightcap somewhere on/near Wellington, then call it

blocks.text: **Real date-night mini-plan:** meet in Verdun → waterfront walk at Parc Arthur-Therrien → Giwa terrasse → post-dinner stroll on Wellington.
Booking & Timing
**Reservations:** Not necessary. Easy to walk in.
**Best time for dates:**

items: **Early dinner:** calmer, more intimate
**Later dinner:** more energy, more “night out” momentum

blocks.text: Date Type Fit

**First Date:** 4/5
Relaxed vibe, not too expensive-feeling, easy to talk.

**Anniversary:** 3/5
More “cute and casual” than “big occasion,” unless you’re specifically craving Korean.

**Impressing someone who likes food:** 3/5
The plating and technique do a lot of the work, even if the flavors play it a little safe.
Bottom Line
Giwa is a solid Montréal date-night pick when you want Korean food with **clean technique**, **pretty plating**, and a menu that nods to tradition while staying seasonal and local.

Just go in knowing it’s more “polished and approachable” than “big bold flavor bomb.” If you’re expecting the typical Korean flavor profile (louder spice, deeper fermentation, bigger punch), I wouldn’t necessarily recommend it. It’s lighter, subtler, and a bit too toned down for my taste. That said, it’s clean cooking, and the night still feels easy and nice.
**Details**

items: **Address:** 3780 Rue Wellington, Verdun, Montréal, QC H4G 1V2
**Neighborhood:** Verdun (Promenade Wellington)
**Website:** [https://restaurantgiwa.ca/](https://restaurantgiwa.ca/)
**Tip:** Terrasse seating is the best date-night move when the weather’s good.
